content.title: Recap: Texas basketball falls to UCLA in another Final Four loss
content.text: PHOENIX — Due to an ice-cold offensive performance in the desert, Texas women's basketball closed out its season Friday night with a loss in the Final Four for the second straight year.Texas shot just 30.8% from the field in the 51-44 loss to UCLA at the Mortgage Matchup Center. The seven-point defeat ends the Longhorns' season with a 35-4 record and extends the program's championship drought to 40 seasons.Article continues below this adGet Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.ONLY 25¢Texas, which entered Friday's semifinal with a 12-game winning streak, had embraced a "punch first" philosophy over the course of its NCAA Tournament run. After the Longhorns had jumped out to a 16-3 lead over South Carolina in last month's SEC Tournament championship game, UT forward Justice Carlton even said "I do really enjoy that punch-first mentality."Texas Longhorns forward Justice Carlton (11) is guarded during the NCAA Final Four game against UCLA at the Mortgage Matchup Center on Friday, April 3, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona.Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-StatesmanDuring its three wins at the SEC Tournament and in the first four rounds of the NCAA Tournament, Texas averaged 12.3 points over the first five minutes of those games. It allowed an average of 5.3 points the opening five minutes of those games against Alabama, Ole Miss, South Carolina, Missouri State, Oregon, Kentucky and Michigan. Just one team held a lead over Texas at the five-minute mark of a first quarter, and UT eventually turned that 13-10 deficit into a 100-58 victory.Article continues below this adBut this time, Texas was unable to punch first. In fact, the Longhorns kept swinging and missing.Over the first five minutes, Texas went 2-for-5 from the field with two turnovers while mustering a measly four points. That start led to a 9-4 hole for UT to dig itself out of. Texas went on to score a season-low six points in the first quarter. The Longhorns faced a 20-17 deficit at halftime against a UCLA team that wasn't faring any better on offense.Texas didn't warm up after the halftime break, but seven points from Carlton in the third quarter's final 91 seconds kept the Longhorns in the game. Texas fell behind by 13 points in the fourth quarter, but Jordan Lee led a late comeback attempt that got UT within 47-44. However, UCLA center Lauren Betts' block of a late layup attempt by Madison Booker sealed the Longhorns' fate.Article continues below this adIn her final game in a Texas uniform, senior guard Rori Harmon contributed eight points, five rebounds and five assists. Texas also got 11 points from Kyla Oldacre and seven points from both Lee and Carlton, but Booker's All-American campaign ended with a 3-for-23 shooting performance.UCLA was led by Betts' 16 points and 11 rebounds while Kiki Rice added 11 points. UCLA (36-1) advances to play South Carolina (36-3) in Sunday's national championship game. Texas vs. UCLA: Live updates, highlights 4th (15.1): UCLA 47, Texas 44 Texas got a defensive stop, but Madison Booker was blocked by Lauren Betts on the other end. The Longhorns will need to either foul or force a quick turnover after this timeout if it wants another chance at tying this game.Article continues below this ad 4th (55.8): UCLA 47, Texas 44 Sophomore guard Jordan Lee's seventh point of the fourth quarter has pulled Texas within three points. UCLA has the basketball after this timeout. 4th (3:35): UCLA 45, Texas 37 Can Texas mount one final rally to save its season? Jordan Lee has scored five points in the fourth quarter, but she is the only Longhorn with multiple buckets in the quarter.Article continues below this ad 4th (8:30): UCLA 38, Texas 28 UCLA has scored on its first three possessions of the fourth quarter, and Texas is officially in the danger zone. While the Bruins are 2-for-2 from the field and 2-for-2 from the free-throw line, Texas has missed its only shot of this quarter and also committed a turnover.A Gabriela Jaquez basket off of a UT turnover has forced Vic Schaefer to call a timeout. Pulled with three minutes left in the third quarter, All-American forward Madison Booker remains on the bench for Texas. End 3: UCLA 31, Texas 28 Seven points from Justice Carlton in the final 91 seconds of the third quarter have kept Texas in this game. The Longhorns, though, have been unable to get any closer than one point in the second half.Article continues below this adFor the game, UT is shooting 27.1% from the floor. Texas star Madison Booker, who was just recognized at the Mortgage Matchup Center as the Cheryl Miller Small Forward of the Year, has missed 15 of her 16 shots.Lauren Betts is leading UCLA with her 10 points and 10 rebounds. The Bruins have committed 17 turnovers. 3rd (7:41): UCLA 22, Texas 19 Neither team has heated up after halftime. UCLA has traded a Kiki Rice basket for a Kyla Oldacre score for Texas.Article continues below this ad Halftime: UCLA 20, Texas 17 After falling behind by 10 points in the first half, Texas pulled within three points during two separate parts of the second quarter. But a cool-shooting Texas team was unable to tie the game or take a lead. The Longhorns missed 24 of their 32 shots in the first half as All-American forward Madison Booker was held to a 1-for-12 performance.Texas point guard Rori Harmon heads into halftime with a team-high eight points and four rebounds.UCLA wasn't much better on offense in the first half as the Bruins shot 37.5% from the floor. Gianna Kneepkens leads UCLA with her seven points.Article continues below this adThree things worth noting: With some of its starters struggling, Texas leaned on reserves Aaliyah Crump (12 minutes) and Ashton Judd (10 minutes) in the first half. Neither team shot a free throw in the first half. A total of seven fouls were called. UCLA didn't score over the final 3:35. Texas didn't score over the final 2:27. UCLA guard Kiki Rice (1) is guarded by Texas Longhorns guard Bryanna Preston (1) during the NCAA Final Four game at the Mortgage Matchup Center on Friday, April 3, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona.Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman 2nd (6:42): UCLA 16, Texas 8 Texas is struggling to get back in this game, but UCLA is also struggling to pull away on the scoreboard from the Longhorns. Both teams have scored two points in the second quarter.Article continues below this ad End 1: UCLA 14, Texas 6 Texas has been used to getting off to fast starts, but the Longhorns find themselves in an early hole after the lowest-scoring first quarter of their season. Texas had been averaging 22.1 points in its opening quarters this season, and it had posted 105 first-quarter points over its four NCAA Tournament games, but a 3-for-14 shooting performance in Friday's first quarter held the team's offensive prospects in check. Texas also committed three turnovers over the day's first 10 minutes.In the first quarter, UCLA got five points in the opening quarter from guard Gianna Kneepkens. All-American center Lauren Betts added four points.Article continues below this ad 1st (2:08): UCLA 14, Texas 4 Texas coach Vic Schaefer was just forced to burn a timeout after his team continued to struggle on offense. Texas is shooting just 2-for-9 from the field in the first quarter. Meanwhile, UCLA has made six of its 13 shots with two 3-pointers. 1st (4:29): UCLA 9, Texas 4 Gianna Kneepkens, who visited Texas this offseason following her decision to transfer from Utah, has scored five quick points to give UCLA an early lead in Phoenix. Kneepkens has also grabbed three rebounds.Article continues below this adMeanwhile, Texas is off to a 2-for-6 start on offense.
